newsitem.title: INDIA: India detains controversial Hindu guru in new case.
newsitem.headline: India detains controversial Hindu guru in new case.

text.p: Indian federal investigators on Thursday detained Hindu guru Chandraswami (one name), who has been linked with leading politicians, on suspicion of foreign exchange law violations.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Chandraswami and his secretary, Kailash Nath Agarwal, in a case involving an alleged violation of the Foreign Contributions Regulation Act (FCRA), CBI spokesman S.M. Khan told Reuters.
They were detained because they could not provide documents to explain receipts of nearly 23 million rupees ($642,400) by a religious trust they were associated with, he said.
Chandraswami was later shifted to a hospital after he complained that he was unwell, Khan said.
Asked if they would be charged, he replied, "That will depend on the investigation."
The Supreme Court on Wednesday rejected the guru's efforts to get anticipatory bail to avoid arrest, which can be sought in Indian law by a person who expects to be arrested in a case.

Chandraswami was jailed for five months after the CBI arrested him in May 1996 in a cheating case in which former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao was named as a co-defendant by a court. Chandraswami was later released on bail.

The guru, who counts Hollywood actress Elizabeth Taylor and the Sultan of Brunei among his followers, was also accused of involvement in a forgery case in which Rao was charged with defaming a political rival in 1989.
Rao and Chandraswami have denied wrongdoing in both the cheating and forgery cases. Trials are continuing.

Rao resigned as president of the Congress party last September after a court upheld a summons issued to him in the cheating case in which a London-based businessman claimed he paid $100,000 in 1983 to Chandraswami in a failed bid to secure a newsprint purchase contract from the government.
The businessman, Lakhubhai Pathak, said Rao, who was a government minister in 1983, had been introduced to him by Chandraswami in the context of his effort to win the deal.

Rao was accused in 1989 of maligning V.P. Singh, who later became prime minister, with the help of false documents to show an alleged illegal account in the name of Singh's son in the Carribean island of St. Kitts.
